chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and in his hand was a dyeing-box wherein was basil.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: A title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.رَيْحَانٌ: Basil, a fragrant herb often used in traditional medicine and for dyeing.
key_terms.مِخْضَبَةٌ: A small container or box used for holding henna or other substances for dyeing hair or beard.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq hold in his hand when Yunus ibn Ya'qub visited him?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi highlights the natural simplicity of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who used basil (rayhan) for hair dyeing, a practice reflecting both the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams' preference for pure, natural substances. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is often cited to validate the permissibility of using plant-based dyes, emphasizing that such adornment is not only allowed but can be an act of following the Imams' refined yet unpretentious lifestyle.
